question: Can a new pod reach destinations its NetworkPolicy denies before k3s's embedded kube-router programs its egress rules, do connections opened then outlive enforcement, and does an admission-injected egress gate close both without stalling ci and project workloads?

finding.engine: k3s v1.36.3+k3s1 embedded network policy controller, kube-router v2.6.3-k3s1, flannel wireguard-native over tailscale0; no k3s flag closes the window or flushes conntrack (also true of v1.36.4+k3s1 and v1.37.0+k3s1)
finding.held_connection: lab (k3d, same k3s): a TCP connection opened at t=0 to a denied server still carried requests at 5 s and 60 s while fresh connections were refused, because KUBE-NWPLCY-COMMON accepts ESTABLISHED,RELATED ahead of the policy chains
finding.gvisor: no protection: runsc network=sandbox traffic crosses the same host netfilter; 16 of 18 gVisor lab pods raced and kept held connections
finding.exposure: C2 or exfiltration from pods isolated from the internet, cloud metadata, unauthenticated API server and kubelets (401), node metrics over the tailnet, kube-system pods; CI PR steps start after enforcement and cannot reach the window

host_rule.rule: platform_host forward: ip saddr 10.42.0.0/16 ip daddr 169.254.0.0/16 drop
host_rule.verification: from a pod after apply: cloud metadata times out, cluster DNS resolves

commits.56d7e15f: canary and canary egress policy in every ci and project namespace
commits.c199d6c7: project Flux artifacts carry the netpol-gate/egress component

gate.proof: on one canary: 8080 open, 8081 refused with ECONNREFUSED, 8080 open; timeouts and other errors hold; no deadline
gate.scope: ci and project tier namespaces: ci-infra, ci-nsql, ci-packages, llunde, llunde-pyparser, portfolio, y

canary_verification.10.43.0.21: egress policy enforced in 306ms after 5 attempts; held 4x because a canary accepts its denied port
canary_verification.10.43.0.22: egress policy enforced in 298ms after 3 attempts; held 2x because a canary accepts its denied port

project_tier.gate: egress policy enforced in 382ms after 5 attempts; held 4x because a canary accepts its denied port

ci_tier.gate: egress policy enforced in 393ms after 5 attempts; held 4x because a canary accepts its denied port
ci_tier.job: check.yml validate, run 36350999555, job 108709567079, success on the gated runner

production_verification.flux: every Kustomization Ready; platform-projects suspended by the Flux artifact cutover, unrelated

lab_qualification.cluster: k3d, k3s v1.36.3+k3s1, gVisor release-20260907.0, runc and gVisor pods
lab_qualification.without_gate: 44-48 failed checks; every pod reached the API VIP, a kubelet and an unpoliced pod and kept its held connection
lab_qualification.with_gate: 0 failed checks; gates held 1-2 attempts (21-91 ms) before passing
lab_qualification.api_lag_2s: ungated 3 of 3 raced; gated, hostAliases and custom-nameserver pods 0 of 9 raced (held 7-16 s); 20 s of dropped probes to 8081 held 3 of 3, then 0 raced
lab_qualification.standalone_kube_router_v2_11_1_netpol_de: 0 of 12 pods raced; each pod's DNS refused for its first ~55 ms

mutations: 48 of 48 killed, including the reviewer's F10 list and the R1 survivors
limitations: A MutatingAdmissionPolicy or ValidatingAdmissionPolicy takes about a second to take effect after creation; pods created in that second start ungated
F9: a new pod that reuses a gated pod's IP before kube-router's delete sync can inherit that pod's chain and pass the gate early
A commit that changes go.mod or MODULE.bazel starts infra-fast from a cold test cache and can overrun its 10 s budget (74bdd743: 10.23 s, rerun 5.39 s)
Established connections survive any later NetworkPolicy change on running pods
Platform-tier pods keep the start window
Removal trigger: k3s#14711, a k3s release exposing kube-router --netpol-default-deny; see the runbook's Egress policy gate removal row
